links.reason: Both turn on a leaf skirt given by the lover (தழை தந்தனனே; தண்தழை விலையென நல்கினன் நாடே), and Natrinai 359 does set the danger of wearing it (உடுப்பின் யாய் அஞ்சுதுமே). But Ainkurunuru 147 only says he gave his country as the price of the leaf skirt, a hyperbole of the gift; nothing in its three lines makes விலை a bride price or places it at the end of secret love, so the 'both ends' arc is the proposer's construction.

Both are war-camp speeches turning on whether the wife knows his pain: யாம்உறு துயரம் அவள் அறியினோ நன்றே against நந்நோய் தன்வயின் அறியாள். Akananuru 304 voices the reproach she must be making (அறவர் அல்லர் நம் அருளாதோர்), which does give the bare wish of 441 a specific motive; 441's line 1 (ஐய ஆயின செய்யோள் கிளவி) is obscure but does not undercut the pairing.

The pairing rests on a real shared point, not just topic: Kuruntokai 340 ends on அவர் இருந்த என் நெஞ்சு, the heart where he dwells, which still goes out to him (காதலர்ப் படர்ந்து) and back to her (நம்மோடு ஆகி), as Kural 1249's heart with the lover inside goes seeking him (உள்ளத்தார் காதலவரால் ... யாருழைச் சேறி). The kandal swaying with ebb and flood (கழிபெயர் மருங்கின் ஒல்கி ஓதம் பெயர்தரப் பெயர்தந்தாங்கு) does turn the couplet's paradox into an ongoing state.

A named puram event in two akam similes: the rain cloud flashes like the drawn swords of Chezhiyan's camp at Alankanam (ஆலங்கானத்து ... செழியன் பாசறை உறை கழி வாளின் மின்னி) and more often than the spear he raised there (ஆலங் கானத்து அமர்கடந்து உயர்த்த வேலினும் பல்ஊழ் மின்னி). The note reports both accurately, and the different speakers and uses (the friend's வருவர் against the woman's reminder of his promise) are as the poems give them; 'stock sign' is a mild overstatement from two cases.

The shared dance names are real (கொடுகொட்டி, பண்டரங்கம் in Kalittokai 1; கொடிகட்டி பாண்டுரங் in Tirumanthiram 2733). But Kalittokai 1 presents them as Shiva's own dances with the goddess keeping time, not as 'stage dances' of a human repertoire, and 2733's lines 2 and 3 are too unclear to support 'files into a yogic doctrine'; the conclusion that the later list inherited a performance repertoire rather than a vision goes beyond both texts.

The shared wording is real: இரும்பிணர்த் துறுகல் பிடிசெத்துத் தழூ (239) against இரும்பிணர்த் தடக்கையில் ஏமுறத் தழுவ (78), though இரும்பிணர் qualifies the boulder in one and the trunk in the other. Both are reproaches for absence, and the teaches is true and specific (the beast's care for its mate versus its blind longing without her), but neither poem limits or adds a condition to the other; it is a same-image link.

The verbal match is close: மேல்வரும் களிற்றொடு வேல்துரந்து (274) and கைவேல் களிற்றொடு போக்கி (774), the spear sent off with the elephant, followed in both by the warrior's own body taking the next weapon (மெய்க்கொண்டனனே; மெய்வேல் பறியா). The note hedges correctly on 274's uncertain last lines, and the couplet as a compression of the heroic scene is shown by the pair; the claim about the whole chapter is a little broad.

The Tamil of 922 ends வரிப்பருந்திண்சிலையே(ன்) உமராயின் மறைகுவனே, which matches Natrinai 362's அமர் வரின் அஞ்சேன் பெயர்க்குவென் நுமர் வரின் மறைகுவென் in both halves: fight strangers, hide from her kin. The note's reading of 922 is the plain one (the marker's 'will not hide' needs a lost negative), so the claim that the kovai kept the udanpokku boast with its exact limit is supported by the words.

A real shared picture of Venkatam: புன்தலை மடப்பிடி இனையக் கன்றுதந்து ... மன்றத்துப் பிணிக்கும் ... வேங்கடங் கிழவோன் (389) and கறைஅடி மடப்பிடி கானத்து அலறக் களிற்றுக் கன்று ஒழித்த ... பதவுமுதற் பிணிக்கும் ... வேங்கடம் (83). The note describes both correctly (different lords, Athanungan and Pulli), and the teaches names what each genre does with the scene: a mark of the lord's land in puram, the frontier crossed in the man's paalai thought.

Both refuse the bard sent by the marutham husband, a stock situation. The two arguments do differ as the note says: a wasted errand like selling needles in the smiths' street (கொல்சேரி நுண்துளைத் துன்னூ விற்பாரின்) against a public warning about his பொய் பொதி கொடுஞ் சொல். But neither limits the other, so QUALIFIES does not fit, and the pair yields little beyond two stock forms of the refusal.

The figure is shared: நாண் எனும் தொல்லை அணி and அணிஅன்றோ நாணுடைமை. But the Kural's நாண் is the worthy man's shame at wrong, and the fragment's is a bride's modesty; and neither verse ranks it above jewels or restraint above pride (தொல்லை is 'ancient', not 'higher', and 1014 says pride without shame is a disease). The teaches adds a ranking the Tamil does not make.
links.text_issue: Paripadal thirattu 6 line 3 has a lacuna after நல்நுதலை.

links.reason: Kural 980's அற்றம் மறைக்கும் பெருமை is exactly what Kalittokai 44 shows: the girl hid his அருள் இன்மை from the friend, the street and her companions (என்னையும் மறைத்தாள் ... சேரியும் மறைத்தாள் ... ஆயமும் மறைத்தாள்), ashamed that others would blame him, and is praised as அனை அரு பண்பினான் நின் தீமை காத்தவள். That the friend turns the praise into a reproach is in the poem's structure, so the teaches is specific and true.

Both girls speak about the lover's night visit during the veri rite, and they take opposite views: 22 laughs because he came (நோய்தணி காதலர் வர), while 360 prays வாரற்க தில்ல ... இரவினானே. That is two speakers in two situations, not incompatible claims about one thing, so TENSION does not fit; the teaches is accurate as a contrast.

Both join water-play and an oath at a Murugan shrine (தலை தொட்டேன் தண் பரங்குன்று; அலைவாய்ச் செருமிகு சேஎயொடு உற்ற சூளே). But in Akananuru 266 the oath is the one he swore to her earlier and has broken, not his answer to the water-play charge, and lines 88-96 of Paripadal 6 contain no reconciliation brokered by others; the teaches rests on both of these.

A distinctive shared scene: a female monkey and a wild cow's udder (மந்தி முலைவருடக் கன்றமர்ந்து ஆமா சுரக்கும்; துஞ்சு பதம் பெற்ற ... மந்தி ... வீங்கு சுரை ஞெமுங்க வாங்கி ... பிழியும்). The contrast the teaches draws is in the Tamil: in Natrinai the cows are asleep and the milk is wrung, in the venba the cow lets it down as if for her calf, and the two speakers' purposes (warning before harvest; refusing to part) fit each use.

The verbal frame is shared and specific: மடவது அம்ம ... எழிலி ... வரல் வாரா அளவை (316) against மடவ மன்ற ... கொன்றை ... பருவம் வாரா அளவை (66), each the friend's mullai comfort that calls the rain false. Moving the folly from the konrai that believes the rain to the cloud that sends it is a real development the pair shows.

Hair likened to the shining ripples of a river is shared (அரிசில் அம் தண் அறல் அன்ன இவள் விரி ஒலி கூந்தல்; கான்யாற்று அவிர்அறல் போன்றே), and each names a chieftain's river. But அறல் for dark hair is a common figure, and the teaches makes 'the two ends of the girl's story' out of two unrelated poems: 141 is a man refusing to go for wealth, not a lover kept from eloping.

Same poet, and both ask about துறந்தோர்: தமியராக இனியர் கொல்லோ (172) and வன்பராகத் தாம் சென்ற நாட்டே (180). But the speakers (heroine, friend), thinai (neythal, paalai) and situations differ, and nothing orders them as the start and turn of one absence; the narrative arc in the teaches is imposed.

The near-identical closing line (கோடுயர் பிறங்கல் மலை இறந் தோரே; நிலையுயர் பிறங்கல் மலைஇறந் தோரே) after the same bodily signs (பணைத்தோள், bangles loosening: நெகிழ / ஞெகிழ) is a real formula. The teaches' structural point is visible in the Tamil: 185 fills the space between the signs and the formula with the iron simile and the summer scene of bamboo and ilavam.

270 explains the many have-nots by too few practising austerity (நோற்பார் சிலர்); 377 says even those who amassed crores enjoy only as வகுத்தான் apportioned. They are not about the same fact: one is why people lack, the other is enjoyment of wealth already gathered, and the note does not say which reading the conflict needs (austerity read as past-life merit makes them agree).

The two images do run opposite ways: Kalavazhi 30 likens the battlefield's blood to a hill-torrent rolling boulders (மலையுருட்டு நீர்போல் தடங்கொண்ட ஒண்குருதி), while Paripadal 12 sees the Vaiyai's monsoon water red with blood and names it the river of the killing army (கார் அடு காலை கலிழ் செங் குருதித்தே போர் அடு தானையான் யாறு). The pairing shows the reversibility that neither verse shows alone.

The attitudes do differ: the Kural's man welcomes ஊரறிந்த கெளவை as having what he has not yet got, while in Natrinai 4 அலரே அன்னை அறியின் ... அரிய ஆகும் and the friend turns it into a demand for marriage. But different speakers in different situations is not a tension, and the teaches itself resolves the difference (it depends on who bears the cost); as a qualification it holds.

Both women stop a man's oath by the god: Paripadal 8 forbids swearing by Murugan because அருள் இல் அணங்கான் மெய் வேல் தின்னும், and Natrinai 386 has அணங்குடை அருஞ் சூள் தருகுவென் met with நும்மோர் அன்னோர் துன்னார் இவை. The contrast is specific, but it rests on reading the line in 386 as the girl's refusal of his oath, which the Tamil does not fix and the marker flags as uncertain; the speech turns in Paripadal 8 are also uncertain.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 8 line 52 has a lacuna and line 51 was taken for a heading in the source.

links.reason: Kural 1151 accepts only செல்லாமை, and Natrinai 256 says exactly that, twice: இந் நிலை தவிர்ந்தனம் செலவே ... தண் படு கானமும் தவிர்ந்தனம் செலவே. That he renounces both the burnt forest and the cool forest of the rains is in the poem, so the teaches' point about what makes the promise credible is specific and true.

Both use the nerunji (ஞாயிறு அனையன் ... நெருஞ்சி அனைய என் பெரும்பணைத் தோளே; நெருஞ்சிக் கட்கின் புதுமலர் முட்பயந்தாங்கு), but for different points: the plant turning to the sun, and the flower followed by thorns. 315 does not 'already hold the pain' 202 states; nothing in its four lines mentions thorns or change, so the teaches overreads it.

Both measure by immensity (நிலத்தினும் பெரிதே வானினும் உயர்ந்தன்று; மருங்கு அறிவாரா மலையினும் பெரிதே), but this is a common hyperbole, applied in one to the bond and in the other to the grief. Kalittokai 48 does not answer or turn Kuruntokai 3, so 'one quantity' and 'turns the heroine's boast into a charge' are the shared figure dressed up.

The two refusals treat the meeting times differently: Kuruntokai 217 leaves the day open (தினைகிளி கடிகெனிற் பகலும் ஒல்லும்) and fears only the night, while Thinaimalai 59 closes both (பகல்வரின் கவ்வை பலவாம் ... இரவரின் ஏதமும் அன்ன). The later poem adds a condition to the earlier, and the step to marriage as the only way left is implicit in it.

Both quote a maxim of men's work only to overrule it: வினையே ஆடவர்க்கு உயிரே completed by மனையுறை மகளிர்க்கு ஆடவர் உயிர் (135), and அருள் அன்று ஆக ஆள்வினை ஆடவர் பொருள் refuted as பொருள்அல் காட்சி (75), with the man staying in both (அழுங்குவர் செலவே; பிரியச் சூழ்தலும் உண்டோ). The teaches names a specific shared strategy.

The idea is the same and specific: இன்மை உரைத்தார்க்கு அது நிறைக்கல் ஆற்றாக்கால் தன் மெய் துறப்பான் (43.26-27) against சாதலின் இன்னாதது இல்லை இனிதது ஊஉம் ஈதல் இயையாக் கடை. The song's effect on the girl (வாடிய மென் தோளும் வீங்கின ... அளித்தக்கால் போன்றே) supports the claim that the praise itself works the cure.

Kalittokai 125 opens with the Kural's own idea in close wording: நெஞ்சு அறிந்த கொடியவை மறைப்பினும் ... நெஞ்சத்துக் குறுகிய கரி இல்லை, beside தன்நெஞ்சு அறிவது பொய்யற்க ... தன்நெஞ்சே தன்னைச் சுடும். The friend then uses it to charge the lover (அன்பு இலை என வந்து கழறுவல்), so the maxim as rhetoric in akam is shown by the pair.

The connection is real: Kapilar names the Mullur king in both, once as giver of chariots more than the rain on Mullur (123) and once as a raider whose victims' ruin measures the girl's (முள்ளூர் மன்னன் மா ஊர்ந்து எல்லித் தரீஇய இன நிரைப் பல் ஆன் கிழவரின் அழிந்த இவள் நலனே). But the teaches' claim that the praised gifts came from such raids is in neither poem, and the akam simile here is used for the ruin of the girl's beauty, not as a judgment on the king.

The body-as-float image is shared (எம் தோள்புரை புணையே; மார்புபுணை யாக), and both bring in a king's weapon. But in Akananuru 312 the king's spear is likened to the lightning, not the flood, and the 'woman drawing him away' in Ainkurunuru 78 is one reading of an unattributed speaker; the claimed symmetry of marriage-making and marriage-straining is weaker than stated.

The image is shared (இரலை பிணைதழுவ; அண்ணல்இரலை அமர்பிணை தழீஇ), but the stag embracing his doe in the rains is a stock mullai sign, and Kainnilai 29 has lost its application. Supplying the meaning of the lost lines from one Akananuru poem is a guess that any mullai poem would equally support, so the pair teaches only the convention.
links.text_issue: Kainnilai 29 lines 1, 3 and 4 are lost or partly lost.

links.reason: The venba uses the couplet's own phrase (மருள்மாலை) for the same evening with the same failing life (மாயும்என் மாயா உயிர்; உள் நிலாது என்ஆவி ஊர்ந்து). It adds what makes the evening bewildering, the moon picking a quarrel and pouring moonlight to bring back day (இகல்கருதித் திங்கள் ... பகல்வர வெண்ணிலாக் காலும்), so the teaches is specific and true.

Both call her medicine (மருந்தெனின் மருந்தே; தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து), but Kuruntokai 71 lacks the couplet's paradox that she is the cure of the sickness she causes. The turn to an argument against leaving for wealth depends on the paalai colophon and one sense of வைப்பு; the poem itself praises the girl and says nothing about going.

The lexical point is useful: Natrinai 224 uses தெளித்தல் for the man's assurance (பிரியலம் என்று தெளித்தோர்) in a spring poem, which supports reading தெளிக்கும் in Ainkurunuru 350 as his promise. But the 350 line rests on a repaired reading, and season set against promise is common in paalai; 'a fixed pair' generalises from two poems.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 350 line 3 is a repaired reading.

links.reason: The koel of spring marking a broken promise is shared (செங்கண் இருங்குயில் நயவரக் கூஉம் இன்இள வேனிலும் வாரார்; வலந்தசொல் எல்லாம் ... பொய்த்த குயில்), but this is a stock paalai sign. The teaches depends on taking பொய்த்த குயில் as the bird making his words false, a reading the Tamil does not fix (the koel's call may itself be the false thing).

Both address a natural thing as a fellow sufferer (யார் அணங்குற்றனை கடலே; புன்கண்ணை ... நின் துணை வன்கண்ணதோ), a common device. The teaches makes a fair contrast, that the poem grounds the sympathy in her waking at midnight (நள்ளென் கங்குலும் கேட்கும் நின் குரலே), but that point comes from Kuruntokai 163 alone and the connection is mostly the shared device.

The heart going to him is shared (அவர்வயிற் சாரல் நீளிடைச் செலவா னாதே; யாருழைச் சேறி என் நெஞ்சு), and the contrast between marvelling and mocking is real. But Kuruntokai 153 lacks the couplet's key point that he is already within, and 'the couplet's wit rests on an older picture' is a claim about sources that the pair cannot show.

The closing line is identical (உள்ளேன் தோழி படீஇயர் என் கண்ணே), each after a bird-loud shore, and the teaches correctly calls it a formula placed after different shore pictures. Neither poem develops the other; it is a shared formula, and the readings of what each scene does (past play, roosting birds) are interpretation.

The idea of his chest as common property is shared and specific: மார்பு பழனம் ஆகற்க against எல்லாரும் கண்ணின் பொதுஉண்பர் ... நின் மார்பு. But the teaches places the Ainkurunuru wish 'before marriage', which the poem does not say (it is a marutham wish beside the mother's wishes for the king), so the before-and-after story is overstated.

290 names the counsel it answers (காமந் தாங்குமதி என்போர்), but in Akananuru 45 the counsel to endure comes from the colophon thurai (வற்புறுக்குந் தோழிக்கு), not the poem. The contrast of registers is fair (கல்பொரு சிறுநுரை போல மெல்ல மெல்ல இல்லாகுதும் against ஆதிமந்தி போலப் பேதுற்று), but it is two responses to a stock situation, and neither limits the other.

The shared image is real and distinctive: the boar with a striped young that lost its mother (புலிகொல் பெண்பால் பூவரிக் குருளை ... கேழல் புரக்கும்; தாஅய் இழந்த தழுவரிக் குருளையொடு ... கேழல் உறங்கும்), and 265 does explain 268's motherless young. But both are in the boar decade, where a shared creature is expected, and the 'once against a lover' contrast is not in 268, which does not say whether he is husband or lover.

poems.note: The only nature image is the paired kuvalai flowers, joined to her eyes by அன்ன, an open simile.
The peacock scratching where the boar has dug is a single scene that cannot be split into two clear matches with the lovers.
The tusker's trampling and the crushed vengai still flowering within reach map to his hurt and her yielding; the vengai alone could also be read as an iraicchi carrier.

iraicchi.act: the heifers come home at evening close beside the good bull
iraicchi.sense: the cattle returning together mark the hour at which he too should be home with the wife he left lonely

poems.note: The bull-taming is the poem's literal event and its similes are open, so there is no hidden vehicle.
The cloud's coming is the season sign, and the poem states the contrast with his chariot openly.

ullurai.anchor: ஒருநின் பாணன் பொய்ய னாக உள்ள பாணர் எல்லாம் கள்வர் போல்வர்

poems.note: Condition 2 is hard here: the poem states the human case (one lying bard makes all bards seem thieves) but never joins it to the fish that fears the lotus bud.
The buffalo spoiling the lilies looks like a marutham vehicle, but neither the poem nor a thurai states the love situation it would point to.
